slides.0.title: Level 1 review
slides.0.subtitle: Four questions that sum up Tunisia
slides.1.title: Review with four questions
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Where?
slides.1.highlights.0.content: All in the north: the Cap Bon peninsula, south of the capital, the northern valleys and Thibar in Béja to the west
slides.1.highlights.1.title: How did it rise and fall?
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Carthage's Mago left writings; the protectorate produced for France; after independence the state took control, and foreign capital came in from the late 1990s
slides.1.highlights.2.title: What is in the glass?
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Mostly rosé and red, with Carignan and other southern French grapes as the tradition; Kélibia's Muscat of Alexandria is the signature
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Who makes it?
slides.1.highlights.3.content: The UCCV cooperative union at about two-thirds, plus a few joint ventures; exports go mainly to Germany and France
slides.1.content: If you can answer these four in your own words, you are ready for the regulations.

Muscat de Thibar is registered for the same products.
What is the UCCV's place in the industry?

C. Vineyards switched to table grapes
